newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen firmer, but recovery limited.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen firmer, but recovery limited.

text.p: The dollar is likely to drift higher against the yen after falls to 124.60 yen overnight, but its recovery could lack strength amid bearish sentiment and slow demand from Japanese investors, dealers said.
"A continued bearish sentiment is making it difficult for traders to open up long positions, which could limit the dollar's recovery to around 125.60 yen," a bank dealer said.

Possible falls in Tokyo stocks and rises in bond prices after sharp falls in U.S. stocks could lend support to the dollar, but the market is likely to be led by options-linked trading by U.S. funds, a trust bank dealer said.
The dollar firmed to around 125.35 yen in early Asian trade due to short-covering by U.S. funds. It ended at around 125.05/10 yen in New York on Wednesday.

The trust bank dealer said U.S. funds have been actively buying one-month dollar put options with strikes of 124 yen and below. They have tended to cover dollar short positions after sales to take profits, he added.

"Recent trading has been mainly driven by U.S. fund operators who are taking advantage of their options positions." Dealers said Japanese institutional investors were less keen to buy dollars, even below 125 yen.
Some life insurers bought dollars at the low 125 yen level on Wednesday in Tokyo, but many remained cautious about fresh foreign bond investments given the current dollar/yen rate.
Japanese importers are keen to pick up dollars below 125 yen, the city bank dealer said.
Concerns about dollar-selling intervention could continue to overshadow the dollar.
Japan's Kyodo news agency quoted an international monetary source as saying on Wednesday that Japan, the United States and Germany are exploring the possibility of joint dollar-selling intervention.
